picks.title: Donald Rothberg: Dukkha and the End of Dukkha: The Core Teaching of the Buddha
picks.summary: (Insight Meditation Community of Berkeley) The Buddha famously said, "I teach dukkha [suffering or reactivity or a sense of unsatisfactoriness] and the cessation of dukkha.” We explore this core teaching as it is expressed in the Four Noble Truths and the teachings of the Two Arrows and Dependent Origination, including ways that it can be confusing. We suggest ways to understand and implement this teaching both in formal meditation and in everyday life. (See document 328 below, on "Four Meanings of Dukkha, and Contact to Grasping in the Dependent Origination Model.")
picks.reason: Detailed exploration of dukkha and its cessation in Buddha's core teaching.

picks.title: 9/3/26- "No Form" (Heart Sutra)
picks.summary:
Sangha member John Wilhelm shares a talk on emptiness. What the section about "having no form, no feelings, no perceptions, no impulses, no consciousness, no eyes, no ears, no nose, no tongue, no body, no mind..." is pointing us toward.
This continues the exploration of the central Zen text of the Heart Sutra. The source text the group is working with is Shohaku Okumura's Living by Vow Chapter 6 in the section "Emptiness in Practice". Shared at the Crooked River Zen regular sitting in Cleveland, Ohio on 9/3/26.
picks.reason: A talk on emptiness based on the Heart Sutra from a Zen perspective.

picks.title: Ep 182 - The Three Poisons
picks.summary: On the latest episode of The Road Home podcast, we dive into one of the deepest and most crucial teachings of Buddhist philosophy of the mind: the three poisons. These could also be called the three confused habitual responses to the present moment. In this dharma talk, we go "under the hood" of how our moment by moment experience unfolds, and how our observation of our confusion can be simplified to the exploration of three simple momentary experiences, as well as our three confused reactions to them. picks.title: The Open Gate
picks.summary:
In this Wednesday Night Dharma Talk, Sensei Fushin turns to the first two folds of the Eightfold Path—right view and right intention—the wisdom from which the rest of the path grows. Right view, he suggests, is not a belief we acquire but seeing what is actually here, before we add our story about it. “The eye opens. The heart leans,” he says — one sees, one moves, and they are not two.
Source
picks.reason: Sensei Fushin discusses right view and intention, foundational Buddhist ethical teachings.

11 August 2026
Peter Harvey joins the BSWA Boundless Meditation Group online live. BSWA Boundless Meditation Group (previously the Armadale Meditation Group or AMG) teaches you about meditation. The classes generally begin with chanting the Metta Sutta, meditation instructions, meditating together, asking questions, and, if time allows, a Dhamma talk. These weekly Tuesday night teachings are via Zoom from Bodhinyana or Dhammasara Monastery. picks.title: Buddhism as Virtue Ethics (Culture of Awakening Project #1)
picks.summary:
The Culture of Awakening Project is an ongoing exploration of the Buddha's teachings from a socioculltural perspective. Given the naturalistic method of my research, this exploration engages a lot of scholarly disciplines besides Buddhist studies, including linguistics, sociology, anthropology, evolutionary science, primatology, philosophical ethics, social psychology and others. The claims made here are provisional; some are likely to be revised as the exploration proceeds, until the results are published. Please visit me at cintita.org to participate in discussion.

picks.title: What to Love in Everything (Listening Practice) w/ Dave Cuomo
picks.summary: Dave brings us a brass tacks talk on meditation technique with a deep look at listening practice, inner listening, and intentional meditation practice in general. Can we engage in such things without spoiling the freewheeling just sitting shikantaza Zen is famous for? Can we scale the heights of the deepest meditative attainments with nothing but effortless ease? Is the peace we seek waiting quietly for us in the omnipresent roar of the A/C? Find out here!
picks.reason: Practical meditation talk focusing on listening and Zen practice.
